The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let \(N=2100\), and for a prime \(p\), let \(\nu_p(n)\) be the exponent of \(p\) in \(n\).

When two numbers \(a,b\) are replaced by \(\gcd(a,b)\) and \(\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\), for every prime \(p\), the pair of exponents \((\nu_p(a),\nu_p(b))\) is replaced by \((\min(\nu_p(a),\nu_p(b)),\max(\nu_p(a),\nu_p(b)))\). Thus, for each prime \(p\), the multiset of all \(p\)-adic exponents on the board is invariant.

A move changes the board exactly when the chosen numbers are not comparable by divisibility. If \(a,b\) are not comparable, write \(a=gx,\ b=gy\) with \(\gcd(x,y)=1\) and \(x,y>1\). The sum of the two numbers changes from

\[
g(x+y)
\]

to

\[
g+gxy,
\]

an increase of \(g(x-1)(y-1)>0\). Since the total product is invariant, the process must eventually reach a state where no move changes the board.

At that final state, every pair of numbers must be comparable by divisibility; otherwise that pair could be moved and would change the board. So the final numbers form a chain under divisibility. Sorting them as

\[
x_1 \mid x_2 \mid \cdots \mid x_{2100},
\]

we have that for each prime \(p\), the sequence \(\nu_p(x_i)\) is nondecreasing. Because the multiset of \(p\)-adic exponents is invariant, \(\nu_p(x_i)\) must be the \(i\)-th smallest value among

\[
\nu_p(1),\nu_p(2),\dots,\nu_p(2100).
\]

We need the 2026th smallest final number, which is \(x_{2026}\). Since there are 2100 numbers, this is the

\[
2100-2026+1=75
\]

th largest final number.

For a fixed prime \(p\), its exponent in \(x_{2026}\) is the largest \(t\) such that at least \(75\) of the original numbers \(1,2,\dots,2100\) are divisible by \(p^t\). There are

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^t}\right\rfloor
\]

such numbers, so the exponent is

\[
e_p=\max\left\{t:\left\lfloor\frac{2100}{p^t}\right\rfloor\ge 75\right\}.
\]

Because

\[
\frac{2100}{75}=28,
\]

this is equivalent to

\[
p^t\le 28.
\]

Thus:

\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccccccc}
p & 2 & 3 & 5 & 7 & 11 & 13 & 17 & 19 & 23\\
\hline
e_p & 4 & 3 & 2 & 1 & 1 & 1 & 1 & 1 & 1
\end{array}
\]

All other primes have exponent \(0\). Therefore

\[
x_{2026}=2^4\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\cdot 19\cdot 23.
\]

The number of positive divisors is

\[
(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6
=5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot 2^6
=60\cdot 64
=3840.
\]

\[
\boxed{3840}
\]
